title: Noor and the Garden
premise: Ada Galloway fled her hedge-witch mistress to disappear into the Ledgerhouse, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled griefs, borrowed years, names that open doors. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Ada realizes the child's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain by the very guild she serves. To steal it back, Ada must break every rule that kept her safe, ally with a disgraced guild enforcer and the ghost of her dead mistress, and finally pay the price of survival: giving up her own carefully hidden name. In the end, Ada trades her invisibility for the child's freedom, becoming visible—and accountable—at last.
about_author: Lior Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debt records in three countries before turning to fiction. They write about ledgers, ghosts, and the arithmetic of mercy from a small apartment full of unlabeled jars.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She audits the Ledgerhouse's winter accounts, hiding her literacy in old scripts and her past behind meticulous anonymity. A routine entry—a soul sold for three favors—makes her hands shake. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the night of the frost fair, a barefoot girl appears at the guild's back door, speaking a language no living tongue should know. Ada alone half-understands it. The guild master orders the child locked in the cellar 'for assessment.' Beat: dread and reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with fragments of the child's dream-language. Ada brings bread and discovers the girl draws spiraling maps of an underground court. The ledger confirms it: the child's soul was sold as collateral on a guild debt. Beat: guilt igniting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Enforcer's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin, a disgraced guild enforcer who once collected the debt himself, recognizes Ada snooping. Instead of reporting her, he offers uneasy alliance—he owes the child a debt of his own. Beat: wary trust between two people trained to betray.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She studies the Ledgerhouse's charter and finds the loophole: debts may be contested if the collateral can speak its own name. But the child cannot—her name is what was sold. Beat: hope raised and dashed; the shape of the quest emerges.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Desperate for the old scripts, Ada summons the ghost bound in her runaway mistress's grimoire: Mistress Vess herself, bitter and sharp-tongued. Vess agrees to teach her—for a price to be named later. Beat: facing the past she fled.

chapters.title: Lessons in Old Tongues
chapters.summary: Ada's POV interwoven with the child's (rendered as sensation, not words). Vess drills Ada in the pre-kingdom language while the child, watching, corrects her pronunciation by touch. Beat: found family forming in candlelight.

chapters.title: The Frost Fair
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the winter fair, the team gathers supplies and forged papers; Corvin buys the child red boots without explanation. A guild spotter nearly catches them. Beat: brief joy, shadowed by pursuit—the calm before escalation.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The guild master discovers the missing cellar key and accuses Ada publicly. Vess's ghost goes silent when Ada needs her most. Cornered, Ada burns her own ledger page to destroy evidence, severing her safety net forever. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Salt Moor
chapters.summary: Rotating POV: Ada, Corvin, the child. Fugitives now, they cross the salt moor pursued by guild hounds that track names. The child begins speaking again—in fragments of everyone's memories. Beat: exhaustion, bonding, the cost of running made physical.

chapters.title: The Toll-Keeper's Bridge
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A bridge spirit demands a memory as toll. Corvin pays one of his own unprompted—an act of quiet sacrifice that reframes him. Ada learns what he lost collecting the child's debt: his own sworn name. Beat: grief shared is grief halved.

chapters.title: Vess's Price
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ghost finally names her fee: Ada must carry Vess's unfinished business into the mountain court—a confession never spoken in life. Ada accepts. Beat: the theme crystallizes; survival has always had a price, and someone always pays it.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Root
chapters.summary: The child's POV, rendered in her strange clarity. She leads them to the entrance only she can perceive: a door grown into the roots of a petrified forest. It opens to her stolen name's echo. Beat: awe and terror; the child becomes the guide.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The passage down tests each of them with their own hidden ledgers—every unpaid debt made visible. Ada sees her abandoned mistress's face among them. Corvin falters; the child steadies him. Beat: confrontation with the self.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The underground court is beautiful and bureaucratic: souls filed like documents, justice administered as accounting. Ada realizes this place runs on the same logic as the Ledgerhouse—only honest about it. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The court's Auditor offers a trade: the child's soul for Ada's name, freely given. Ada hesitates—not from cowardice, but because she understands what a name means here: total accountability, forever. Beat: the central choice laid bare.

chapters.title: Contested Debt
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Using Vess's teachings, Ada formally contests the original sale before the court, exposing the guild's fraudulent signature. The trial becomes a duel of ledgers. Vess's ghost testifies through Ada's mouth. Beat: rising climax; justice argued outside any lawful court.

chapters.title: The Verdict and the Fire
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The court rules the debt void—but the guild's collectors breach the chamber, torching the archives to erase evidence. In the chaos, the child's soul-shard must be carried out by hand. Corvin holds the door. Beat: climax erupting into action.

chapters.title: What Corvin Owed
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. He stays behind to seal the door against the collectors, paying the last of his debt with his freedom, taken into the court's service. His goodbye is undramatic, almost bookkeeping. Beat: sacrifice rendered in the story's own cold currency—and thus more devastating.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Above ground, Ada performs the restoration Vess taught her: naming the child whole. The girl speaks her true name for the first time—and gives Ada a new one in exchange, chosen freely. Beat: catharsis; the price paid yields something better than safety.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Houses
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Armed with copied evidence, Ada returns to the Ledgerhouse not to hide but to testify, toppling the guild master and forcing reform. She takes Vess's confession to the mistress's grave. Beat: justice institutionalized; ghosts settled.

chapters.title: Noor and the Garden
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue-like. The child—Noor—plants a garden over the sealed mountain door. Ada keeps a new ledger: gifts given, never repaid. Corvin sends a single filed document each season, proof he endures. Beat: quiet resolution; family chosen, debts transformed into care.
